rv.q: It’s a potent piece of theatre, and, in the final words of the C-SPAN moderator, “an interesting and informative hour” that’s highly worth seeing.

Director Daniel Fish, whose dark version of Rodgers and Hammerstein’s “Oklahoma!” similarly featured some distracting avant-garde touches, nevertheless provides a useful historical perspective with this production.
Fish presents all of this material with a directorial flourish that yields moments of surprising humor, a blend of documentary or verbatim theater with elements of theater of the absurd.
Daniel Fish again proves his genuine creative genius with the wildly entertaining and unpredictable Kramer/Fauci.
This production may prove of interest to younger audience members who didn't live through the AIDS crisis but it doesn't hold up as a drama.

cn.t: Critics praise this verbatim staging of the 1993 Kramer-Fauci AIDS debate as absorbing and timely, with controlled fury bringing C-SPAN to vivid life, though some find the format repetitive and undynamic.
